title: Code of Conduct and IT Acceptable Use Policy
sections: Purpose and Scope

This policy establishes the standards of behavior and usage for all individuals accessing Calder Bay Ship Management Ltd systems, including shore-based employees, contractors, and visitors. It ensures the protection of company assets and the integrity of information systems.

All users are expected to comply with this policy at all times. The Code of Conduct and IT Acceptable Use Policy applies to all individuals who use company-owned or controlled devices, networks, software, and data resources.

This includes both internal and external users who have been granted access to these systems. Employees, contractors, and visitors are responsible for using company systems in a manner that aligns with the company’s mission, values, and legal obligations.

This includes adhering to all applicable laws, regulations, and internal guidelines. All users must ensure that their actions while using company systems do not interfere with the operations of the business or the rights of other users.

This includes maintaining the confidentiality and security of company data and resources. The policy covers the use of all digital and physical company assets, including but not limited to computers, mobile devices, printers, servers, and network connections.

Users are required to follow established procedures for accessing and using these resources. The purpose of this policy is to define acceptable use of company systems and to promote a secure, ethical, and productive work environment for all users.
It outlines the responsibilities of each user and the consequences of non-compliance with these standards.
Professional Behaviour
All employees are expected to conduct themselves with professionalism, integrity, and respect in all interactions with colleagues, clients, and third parties at all times.

Employees must treat all individuals with dignity and fairness, regardless of their position, background, or personal circumstances, and must not engage in any form of harassment, bullying, or discriminatory behaviour.

In the workplace, employees are required to maintain a safe and respectful environment by adhering to company policies, reporting any incidents of misconduct, and cooperating fully with investigations.

All employees must respect the confidentiality of company information and the privacy of colleagues, and must not engage in any activity that could compromise trust or create a hostile work environment.

Supervisors and managers are responsible for setting a positive example of professional behaviour, addressing any concerns promptly, and ensuring that all employees understand and comply with the expectations outlined in this policy.

Employees are required to report any incidents of harassment, discrimination, or unethical behaviour to their immediate supervisor or the designated compliance officer without fear of retaliation or reprisal.
Gifts and Conflicts of Interest
Cash gifts are never accepted under any circumstances, and employees must refuse any offer to provide cash gifts directly or indirectly.
Employees must provide detailed information about the source, value, and nature of any gift exceeding USD 50, including any associated documentation or correspondence.
The Compliance department will review all declared gifts and determine if they pose a conflict of interest or violate company policy.
Employees must avoid any situation where personal interests could interfere with their professional duties, including but not limited to accepting gifts that may influence business decisions.
In cases where a gift is accepted in good faith and below USD 50, the employee must still disclose it to their immediate supervisor for record-keeping purposes.
Confidentiality

All employees are required to maintain the confidentiality of all company and client information, including but not limited to operational data, financial records, and communication logs, throughout their employment and for 2 years after employment ends.

Employees must not disclose any confidential information to third parties, including but not limited to former colleagues, contractors, or external auditors, without prior written authorization from the Chief Compliance Officer.

Confidential information must be stored securely using company-approved encryption methods and access controls, and must not be shared via unsecured networks or personal devices unless explicitly permitted by the IT department.
Employees are prohibited from using confidential information for personal gain or to benefit any third party, including but not limited to family members, business associates, or competitors.
Any breach of confidentiality, regardless of intent, will result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment and legal prosecution under applicable laws.
Reporting Concerns
All reports of misconduct must be submitted through the Ethics Hotline, which is the designated internal channel for such concerns.
The Ethics Hotline will acknowledge receipt of all reports within 5 working days, regardless of the nature or severity of the concern.
Employees are encouraged to report any observed or suspected misconduct, including but not limited to unethical behavior, safety violations, or policy breaches.
All reports submitted through the Ethics Hotline are treated with strict confidentiality and are investigated promptly by the designated compliance officers.
Employees who report misconduct in good faith are protected from retaliation and may request a formal review of their case through the compliance officers.
The compliance officers are responsible for ensuring that all reports are acknowledged, documented, and addressed in accordance with the company's policies and procedures.
Passwords and Accounts
All company accounts must use passwords that are at least 12 characters in length. Employees are responsible for ensuring their passwords meet this requirement before accessing any company systems.
Passwords must be changed every 90 days to maintain account security. The system will automatically enforce this requirement and notify users when their password is due for renewal.
Employees are required to store their passwords securely and not share them with anyone, including colleagues or IT support staff. Unauthorized access to company accounts is strictly prohibited.

When creating a new password, employees must avoid using easily guessable information such as names, dates, or common words. Passwords should include a mix of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters.

IT department will monitor account activity and may request password resets if suspicious behavior is detected. Employees must comply with such requests promptly and provide necessary verification to confirm their identity.

All password-related incidents, including suspected breaches or unauthorized access, must be reported immediately to the IT department. Employees are expected to follow established procedures to ensure the integrity of company systems.
Devices and Software

All personal devices used for company business must be registered with IT prior to use, and must remain registered throughout their active use period. IT will maintain a record of all registered devices and ensure compliance with company security protocols.
Employees are prohibited from installing unlicensed software on any company-owned or registered personal devices. Any unlicensed software found on such devices will be removed immediately by IT.

IT will provide employees with guidance on acceptable software usage and will conduct periodic audits to verify compliance with this section. Employees are required to cooperate fully with these audits.

Personal devices used for company business must be configured with the company's security settings, including but not limited to encryption, remote wipe capabilities, and password protection. These settings must be applied before the device is registered with IT.

Employees are responsible for ensuring that any software installed on registered personal devices is compatible with company systems and does not interfere with operational processes. IT will assist in resolving compatibility issues where necessary.
In the event of a security incident involving a registered personal device, the employee must notify IT immediately and provide full access to the device for investigation and remediation.
Email and Social Media

All employees are required to use company-issued email accounts for official business communications and must ensure that all messages are professional, accurate, and free from personal or inappropriate content.
Employees are prohibited from using personal email accounts to conduct company business or to communicate with clients, suppliers, or colleagues unless explicitly authorized by a manager.
Any communication that represents the company's position, services, or activities on social media platforms must be approved in advance by the designated spokesperson or the Head of Communications.
Employees are not permitted to engage in public discussions, posts, or comments that could damage the company's reputation, misrepresent its operations, or disclose confidential information.
When representing the company on social media, employees must use official company accounts and ensure that all content aligns with the company's brand guidelines and legal obligations.
Employees are required to promptly report any unauthorized use of their personal accounts to conduct company business or to make public statements on behalf of the company.
Working While on Leave
Employees on leave are not expected to monitor email or use company systems during their absence.
All communication regarding work-related matters should be directed to the appropriate department head or team lead upon return to active duty.
Employees on leave are responsible for ensuring that any pending tasks are either completed before departure or clearly delegated to a substitute or team member.
The use of company systems, including email, is strictly prohibited during periods of leave unless explicitly authorized by a manager in writing.
Employees on leave must not engage in any work-related activities that could compromise data security or operational integrity.
In the event of an urgent work-related matter during leave, employees are required to contact their manager directly and seek approval before taking any action.
Breaches and Disciplinary Process

Upon identification of a breach of this policy, the employee may respond within 5 working days by submitting a written statement to the Human Resources Department, outlining their position and any mitigating factors.

The Human Resources Department will review the submitted response and consult with the relevant department head to determine the appropriate disciplinary action, which may range from a written warning to dismissal.

The employee is entitled to receive a formal notice of the proposed disciplinary action, including the nature of the breach and the justification for the proposed outcome, prior to any final determination.
The final disciplinary decision will be communicated in writing to the employee by the Human Resources Department, along with details of any appeal process available under this policy.
All disciplinary actions will be documented in the employee's personnel file and may be reviewed during internal audits or investigations as required by company procedures.
